themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: In the semantic context layer answers all three models call conflicting definitions of "customer" a political settlement rather than a modeling gap; agentic traffic answers say agents profit by hiding, and journey orchestration answers say channel owners paid on their own conversions will subvert any central arbiter.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and what you measure often shifts while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers describe stochastic, personalized answers with no denominator; incrementality answers describe platforms changing bidding mid-flight; identity resolution, B2B buying-group intent, and content governance answers all say the validation data or reviewer agreement needed to check the work does not exist.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every safe agent execution answer builds a proxy or gateway that holds the credentials and caps spend, rate, and audience size; the consent enforcement answers put a single checkpoint on every path data leaves the warehouse, and the orchestration answers route all sends through one shared contact ledger or eligibility check.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can estimate whether rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The consent and deletion answers call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removal from a trained model; the incrementality answers say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and the answer engine answers say retrieval and ranking logs are simply not exposed.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. All three models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: The content governance answers say deciding whether evidence supports a claim is a contextual judgment expert reviewers themselves dispute, so the only lever is limiting what can be said; the semantic layer answers say different teams need genuinely different meanings, making governed plurality harder than one dictionary.
